Lessons.Title: Inscribed Angles
ExplanationParagraphs: Learning goal: Prove an inscribed angle subtending an arc is half the corresponding central angle and use it to analyze intersecting chords.
Vertex lies on circle, sides are chords Measure half the intercepted arc not containing vertex
Inscribed angles intercepting same arc are equal Need vertices on same complementary arc Both arc measures referenced properly

Source task parity: after measuring central and inscribed angles to conjecture the half-arc relation, students prove triangles are similar when two chords cross inside a circle. An angle theorem alone or a numeric 90° calculation does not demonstrate this source proof task. Represent the intersecting chords, identify angle pairs intercepting the same arcs, then apply AA similarity.

Source-specific student task: Prove inscribed angle using radii and isosceles triangles, then sketch chord intersection; teacher scores proof. Teacher rubric (0–4): exact labelled construction, valid theorem hypothesis, correct numeric or logical consequences, and a defensible explanation. Original drawings and proofs need teacher review.

KeyConcepts.Title: Inscribed angle

KeyConcepts.Rule: Measure half the intercepted arc not containing vertex

KeyConcepts.Title: Same-arc rule
KeyConcepts.Definition: Inscribed angles intercepting same arc are equal
KeyConcepts.Rule: Need vertices on same complementary arc

KeyConcepts.Title: Intersecting-chord triangle similarity
KeyConcepts.Definition: If chords CB and DE intersect at an interior point F, triangles CFD and EFB can be shown similar by AA using inscribed angles on shared arcs and vertical angles.
KeyConcepts.Rule: The angles FCD and FEB intercept arc DB; FDC and FBE intercept arc CE; the vertical angles CFD and EFB agree.
KeyConcepts.Example: If arcs DB and CE measure 140° and 100°, the corresponding angles at C,E are 70° and at D,B are 50°.

WorkedExamples.Title: Inscribed Angles: AA similarity from two intersecting chords
WorkedExamples.Question: Chords CB and DE intersect at interior F. The intercepted arcs DB and CE measure 140° and 100° respectively. Prove triangles CFD and EFB are similar.
WorkedExamples.Method: Use inscribed angle theorem, the same intercepted arcs, and AA.
Steps: The angles FCD and FEB are inscribed angles intercepting arc DB, so each measures 140°/2=70°.
The angles FDC and FBE both intercept arc CE, so each measures 100°/2=50°.
Thus two pairs of corresponding angles agree; by AA, triangle CFD is similar to triangle EFB (with F↔F as the remaining vertical-angle pair).
WorkedExamples.Answer: Triangles CFD and EFB are similar by AA, with corresponding angle measures 70°,50°,60°.
WorkedExamples.Check: Sum 70°+50°+60°=180°. Each asserted angle pair subtends the same arc; interior intersection and distinct endpoints are required.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Using whole intercepted arc instead of half
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Inscribed angles are half corresponding central angle

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Applying interior chord formula to exterior secants

SummaryPoints: Prove an inscribed angle subtending an arc is half the corresponding central angle and use it to analyze intersecting chords.
Inscribed angles on the same intercepted arc are equal; intersecting chords form AA-similar triangles when corresponding angles subtend the same arcs.
